### Import and Clean Data

Sample data: articles on Xinjiang women

```{r echo = F}
#136596 rows of text
articles_df <-  read_csv("articles_df.csv") |> 
    mutate(year = year(published_date),
           date = published_date)
```

### Load a very small subset: 10 articles

```{r echo=FALSE}

llm_text <- articles_df |> 
  filter(!is.na(sentence)) |> 
  slice(1:1000)

llm_text <- llm_text |> 
  mutate(sentence = gsub("\n", " ", sentence)) |> 
  mutate(sentence = gsub("\\s+", " ", sentence))

```

### Industrial strength cleaning and processing

--Articles put into a single string of text, no punctuation or spaces

```{r echo=FALSE}
process_articles <- function(df) {
  # First group by article identifiers and concatenate sentences
  # Using filename as the identifier, but you might need to use other columns
  compiled_df <- df %>%
    group_by(filename) %>%
    summarize(
      sentence = paste(na.omit(sentence), collapse = " "),
      # consolidating metadata into single row per article
      title = first(title),
      date = first(date),
      year = first(year),
      filename = first(filename)
    )
  
  # lowercase words (preserving spaces)
  compiled_df <- compiled_df %>%
    mutate(sentence = tolower(sentence))
  
  return(compiled_df)
}

# Apply the function to your dataframe
processed_llm_text <- process_articles(llm_text)

# Prepare data with filenames and content
articles_for_analysis <- processed_llm_text %>%
  select(filename, sentence) %>%
  mutate(article_data = paste("FILENAME:", filename, "\nCONTENT:", sentence))

# Combine with clear separators
combined_text_with_filenames <- paste(articles_for_analysis$article_data, 
                                    collapse = "\n\n---ARTICLE SEPARATOR---\n\n")
```

### The AI prompt

```{r echo=FALSE}
chat <- chat_openai(
  model="gpt-5-nano", 
  system_prompt = "
  You are an academic researcher performing context analysis on selected articles. 
  
  Analyze each article and classify it based on these criteria:
  
1. If an article contains two or more mentions of any of the following terms, classify it as 'women':
   - Xinjiang women
   - Uyghur women
   - Muslim women

2. If an article contains two or more mentions of any of the following terms, classify it as 'counter':
   - terror*
   - extrem*
   - radical*

An article can belong to both categories.


  Return ONLY a CSV-formatted result with exactly two columns:
  filename,category
  
  For example:
  filename,category
  filename,counter
  filename2,counter;women
  filename3,women
  
  No additional text, explanations, or summary counts."
)

# Send to the LLM
response <- chat$chat(combined_text_with_filenames)
```

### Process first response

We're taking the chat response and putting it into a dataframe

```{r echo=FALSE}
process_llm_response_to_df <- function(response) {
  # Extract lines
  lines <- strsplit(response, "\n")[[1]]
  
  # Remove markdown code block markers if present
  lines <- lines[!grepl("^```", lines)]
  
  # Initialize vectors for data
  filenames <- c()
  categories <- c()
  
  # Flag to track if we're processing data (after header)
  header_found <- FALSE
  
  for (line in lines) {
    # Skip empty lines
    if (trimws(line) == "") next
    
    # Skip row numbers or other artifacts (lines with asterisks)
    if (grepl("\\*\\*", line)) next
    
    # Check if this is the header line
    if (grepl("filename,category", line, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      header_found <- TRUE
      next
    }
    
    # Process data lines (only after header is found)
    if (header_found) {
      parts <- strsplit(line, ",")[[1]]
      if (length(parts) >= 2) {
        filenames <- c(filenames, parts[1])
        categories <- c(categories, paste(parts[2:length(parts)], collapse=","))
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Create and return the dataframe
  if (length(filenames) > 0) {
    data.frame(
      filename = filenames,
      category = categories,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  } else {
    # Return empty dataframe with correct structure if no data found
    data.frame(
      filename = character(0),
      category = character(0),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }
}

result_df <- process_llm_response_to_df(response)

result_df

```

### Validate results

We're building a spreadsheet for export just with the results

```{r echo=FALSE}
processed1 <- result_df |> 
  mutate(ai_correct = " ",
         ai_wrong = " ",
         unsure = " ",
         notes = " ")

instructions <- tibble(
  filename = c(
    " ",
"If an article contains two or more mentions of any of the following terms, classify it as 'women':",
"   - Xinjiang women",
"   - Uyghur women",
"   - Muslim women",
"If an article contains two or more mentions of any of the following terms, classify it as 'counter':",
   "- terror*",
   "- extrem*",
   "- radical*",
"An article can belong to both categories."

  ) |> str_wrap(width = 60)
)

# 2. Append the instructions to the bottom of your dataset
spreadsheet <- bind_rows(processed1, instructions)

write.csv(spreadsheet, "spreadsheet_ai_verification.csv")


file_paths1 <- processed1$path
processed_list <- lapply(file_paths1, read_lines)
```

### Process AI results

Capture the articles and put them into a single text file, separated by file name


```{r}
# 1. Group by filename, combine sentences into a single text block per file
file_blocks <- llm_text %>%
  group_by(filename) %>%
  summarize(file_content = paste(sentence, collapse = "\n"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pull(file_content)

# 2. Define the separator (two rows of asterisks)
separator <- "\n\n**********\n**********\n\n"

# 3. Collapse all file blocks together with the separator
combined_output <- paste(file_blocks, collapse = separator)

# 4. Write the final string to output.txt
writeLines(combined_output, "output.txt")
```

**Follow these instructions**

1)  Open combined_nixon_files.txt.
2)  Next, create a Google Sheet, import spreadsheet_ai_verification.csv
3)  Read the articles in output.txt
4)  Rate the responses on spreadsheet_ai_verification: ai_correct; ai_wrong; unsure
5)  Now, discuss!
